text: Situations caused by geopolitical conflicts, health and natural disasters.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Singapore has not and will not be spared from such disruptions to their lives.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: We are even more vulnerable because we are a small-nation state and have to punch above our weight to ensure we will not be defeated and will emerge stronger than ever.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: It is, hence, vital that we prepare Singaporeans adequately and in advance for emergencies – from having sufficient essential supplies for our people, to giving timely and correct information to together navigate through such crises.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, I am heartened to note that MINDEF and SAF continue to engage the community and key stakeholders to understand the challenges, constraints and opportunities faced by our people and businesses.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such engagements will go a long way to help boost the public support for defence and enable Singaporeans to better understand defence issues, so that they can play a more active role in building a resilient society.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Over the years, the Advisory Council on Community Relations in Defence (ACCORD) has provided an invaluable avenue for MINDEF and SAF to receive feedback and proposals.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Last year, Senior Minister of State for Defence Mr Zaqy Mohamad provided an update on the various ACCORD initiatives, including ACCORD's focus on engaging youth and women on defence issues.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Chairman, our NSmen form the backbone of Singapore's defence and work tirelessly every day to ensure that they are always ready to respond to any current and future threat against Singapore.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Yet, the continued strength of our defence cannot be predicated on the individual soldier alone.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: For a NS man to carry out his duties effectively and with commitment, the support of his community and family is essential.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Singaporeans from every part of our society must continue to also show appreciation for the hard work that they put in.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: ACCORD plays an integral role, by reaching out to individuals from all walks of life, to strengthen their commitment to defence.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: ACCORD must continue its efforts to engage individuals, corporations and community groups, to mobilise support for defence issues, especially for NS.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: The Singapore Discovery Centre (SDC) is about who we are and what we want to be.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: I am glad that almost two decades on from its last major revamp, the SDC continues to keep Singapore's history alive for our children and grandchildren, and to be a place for interactive learning.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: Over the past two years, Senior Minister of State for Defence, Mr Zaqy Mohamad, has updated the House about plans to refresh and transform the SDC.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: If we do an Internet search on SDC, it currently looks like a tourist attraction, but surely, it must be more than a tourist site.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan
text: How can we use the centre to help our children learn more about our history, and also about our future?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Mr Chairman, a shared sense of belonging is key to a country's identity.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Central to this is a collective understanding and appreciation that citizens have of our country's history.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We recently celebrated Total Defence Day on 15 February.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For many young Singaporeans, it might have seemed like just any other day, except for the public warning siren that was played on that day.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In case we forget, Total Defence Day is commemorated on the day that Singapore fell during World War II.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It is a day to remind ourselves of the lessons from that dark chapter of Singapore's history – that the responsibility to defend our nation lies with all of us.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It is, therefore, crucial that lessons from such key historical moments are passed down to future generations of Singaporeans, who will naturally feel increasingly distanced from long ago events that have shaped our nation.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: To this end, museums are a good medium.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: When my children were younger, I used to bring them to places, such as the Battlebox and the Army Museum, to help them relate to what it was like living at a time where safety could not be taken for granted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister for Defence, Dr Ng, said in his speech, that defence is a long-term business requiring consistent investment over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Aside from building a capable armed forces that can serve as a deterrence and defend us against threats, MINDEF works hard on defence diplomacy and cooperation – both bilateral and multilateral - to build defence ties and address common security challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Mr Shawn Huang and Mr Zhulkarnain asked about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: This Centre promotes research and information sharing among partner nations on emerging cybersecurity and informational threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: ACICE has started sharing products with all partner nations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: The second example is that of the Shangri-La Dialogue (SLD).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: After a two-year hiatus, the SLD resumed last year in a physical format.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Beyond investing in a strong SAF and defence diplomacy, we have continuously invested in and evolved the NS system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NS is the cornerstone of our defence and national security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: NSmen form the bulk of the SAF, the Police and Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Their sacrifices and commitment lay the foundation for Singapore's security and prosperity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It is critical that we continuously maintain and strengthen the NS system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Here, I am happy to inform the House that public support for NS remains very strong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: It shows that Singaporeans understand that small states are inherently vulnerable, that we need to take responsibility for our own defence and that NS remains, I would say more than relevant – it remains critical.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: MINDEF and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) make regular efforts to strengthen the NS system and recognise the contributions of our national servicemen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Last year, the NS Review Committee (NSRC) submitted recommendations to ensure that NS remained effective amidst Singapore's evolving defence needs, as well as the changing needs of our NSmen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: We also commemorated 55 years of NS (NS55).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: Today, I will provide an update on these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
text: To recap, the NSRC's recommendations can be grouped into three broad thrusts.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Members may also access the handout through the MP@SGPARL mobile app.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked about MINDEF's efforts to optimise the deployment of NSmen to maximise their contributions.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Given low fertility rates and shrinking cohort sizes, the SAF needs to optimise the contributions of every soldier – in two ways.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The first concerns medical fitness and job requirements.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: To complement our existing medical screening process, we introduced functional assessments for pre-enlistees with selected orthopaedic conditions.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked for an update on this.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Under this functional assessment, we assess the pre-enlistee's ability to do physical tasks, such as running, jumping and carrying heavy loads.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This approach allows us to accurately match more servicemen to operational roles as compared to the traditional approach of matching servicemen based only on their medical diagnosis.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: At the same time, we are leveraging technology to redesign jobs.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Similarly, this enables more servicemen to be deployed into operational roles.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The second way is to maximise contributions that concern knowledge and skills.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: To keep up with the changing nature of conflict and emerging threats, the SAF needs to grow and tap the skills of our NSmen.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: I have updated the House in recent years about Work-Learn Schemes for NSFs, a subject which Mr Don Wee asked about.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Abdul Samad also asked about career pathways in the SAF related to engineering.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Under the Work-Learn Schemes, NSFs attain a diploma or partial university credits from Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) while performing a period of full-time NS followed by regular service.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: They are trained in domains, such as artificial intelligence, supply chain management and engineering, which allows them to be deployed as digital specialists, supply supervisors and technicians respectively.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Two months ago, we also introduced a new scheme for NSFs to pursue Diplomas in Engineering (Mechanical Technology) and be deployed as Naval Warfare System Specialists.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: By 2025, we expect 500 NSFs to be enrolled in Work-Learn Schemes every year.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Our efforts to maximise expertise cover not only NSFs, but also NSmen.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Some of our NSmen have skills that the SAF needs, which they have acquired in their civilian careers.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The SAF has stepped up efforts to identify and redeploy these NSmen to make better use of their civilian expertise and skills.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked for an update on the results.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This represents a four-fold increase from the average number of 50 NSmen a year between 2014 and 2021.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: New areas to which NSmen were redeployed last year included digital and intelligence, logistics and engineering.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: While optimising deployment is important, we also need to make NS processes more seamless, so that our national servicemen can focus on their training.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked about this.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This brings me to the second thrust of the NSRC's recommendations – that of improving the NS experience.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: A major administrative burden for employers and NSmen had been the filing of Make-Up Pay claims for In-Camp Training (ICT).

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Entries were, therefore, sometimes incomplete and payment delays happened.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: In September last year, we introduced an automated system that draws income-related information from the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Board and Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) to calculate Make-Up Pay amounts.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: If they so wish, employers and NSmen can review the computed amounts and file for adjustments.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Otherwise, the amounts will be paid out automatically and there is no action needed on their part.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: As a result, we have had very positive feedback.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The claim amounts derived from CPF Board and IRAS data have proven to be up to date and accurate.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Since September, 92% of claims have been processed automatically.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Based on our estimates, the automated system will save employers, NSmen, MINDEF and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) more than 260,000 man-hours of processing effort every year.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Apart from saving time, the automation has also allowed us to make payment much faster.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Since September, 90% of claims have been paid within 10 days from the start of in-camp training (ICT).

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Practically, the payment is processed while people may still be undergoing their period of ICT.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Alongside this automated system, we also introduced a base NS pay of $1,600 per month whenever NSmen attend ICT or other ORNS activities.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This means that if the data from CPF Board or IRAS indicates that an NSman earns less than $1,600 per month, MINDEF will top up his NS Pay to $1,600 per month, prorated according to the duration of the ORNS activity.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: As an example, if an NSman attends a 12-day ICT, on a prorated basis of a base pay of $1,600, he would be paid at least $600.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This provides additional support to NSmen who are students or who are not employed or whose income from informal jobs may not be fully captured in CPF or IRAS data.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: We hope that this gives NSmen from lower-income segments greater financial security when they attend ORNS activities.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: On this, I just want to reiterate the point that MINDEF is fully committed to the well-being and welfare of both our NSFs and NSmen.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Through so many examples that we have given, the public can be confident that we will regularly update such benefits, in order to take good care of our servicemen.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Our efforts to digitalise NS transactions and touchpoints go beyond Make-Up Pay claims.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Members who are NSmen would remember receiving physical vouchers from MINDEF and MHA in the past as part of our recognition efforts.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: With the change, national servicemen are now able to receive, carry and redeem their credits via their mobile devices.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The credits can be used with any business that accepts payment by NETS or PayNow QR.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Some businesses also offer our servicemen discounts for the use of the credits as a show of support for NS.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: When they do so, this has effectively further raised the dollar value of the benefits.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This is a relevant piece of data because it shows that when it is made available to be used electronically, it makes it much more convenient and it speeds up the utilisation and the enjoyment of the benefit.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: In comparison, it took 18 months to achieve the same use for physical vouchers when we did that for NS50.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: I encourage all national servicemen to fully utilise your credits.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Ms Poh Li San asked about the use of the OneNS platform to improve the NS experience.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The OneNS platform is a consolidation of NS-related services and transactions into a single mobile app.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: We rolled out the first phase of OneNS to selected ICT units.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: NSmen in these units can register their attendance at ICT easily with the geolocation function on the app.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This has allowed the units concerned to start the proper ICT programme earlier.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: OneNS will be extended to more units in the coming months.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: I now move on to the third thrust, which is that of enhancing recognition and support for NSmen, something which Mr Chong Kee Hiong asked about.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Last year, we conducted a year-long NS55 campaign themed "Generations of Strength".

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi asked about the response to that campaign.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Besides giving the NS55 Recognition Package to eligible NSmen, MINDEF and MHA organised a series of commemorative initiatives that was well received.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: As an example, the NS55 theme song "Back in the Day" accumulated over six million views online.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The showcase at the Army Open House on the evolution of NS attracted 140,000 visitors.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The community came together to organise activities such as walking alongside our NSmen under the NS55 Fitness Challenge.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: All in all, the NS55 campaign achieved its objectives.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Surveys conducted after the campaign showed that 80% of our NSmen felt valued for their contributions to NS.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: And 90% of the general public felt that NS was a source of pride for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: NS55 may have concluded but our efforts to recognise and support our NSmen and their families continue.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: In fact, we can already look forward to the opening of the new Singapore Armed Forces Reservist Association (SAFRA) clubhouse in Choa Chu Kang in May this year.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: That will bring an exciting host of amenities, especially to the 90,000 NSmen who reside in the northwest.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: I think many of us might have seen the exciting photos of my colleague, Senior Minister of State Zaqy's recent hard-hat tour of the upcoming facilities.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Beyond recognition benefits, MINDEF and MHA are also committed to strengthening financial protection for SAF and Home Team servicemen and volunteers.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: We have also extended the coverage to conditions, such as long-term hearing damage and decompression sickness.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: It is, therefore, fitting that the Group Personal Accident insurance is now called Group Personal Injury insurance – to reflect that extended coverage.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: I have covered the three thrusts of the NSRC but these are not our only priorities.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The SAF will always pay particular attention to safe and effective training of our NSmen.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Henry Kwek had asked about this.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: We are investing heavily in our training infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Minister for Defence Dr Ng had spoken about how SAFTI City will allow our NSmen to undergo realistic training for a wide range of scenarios as well as the SAF's plans to leverage technology, including simulators and real-time sensors, to enhance training.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The development of expanded overseas training areas, including those in Australia, will also allow our NSmen to have more opportunities to participate in large-scale, integrated training.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: While training must be realistic to be effective, we will never compromise on safety.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about how the SAF balances safety and training effectiveness.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Sharing of safety practices and co-development of safety management plans have always been an important part of training exercises that SAF conducts, both for itself as well as with other military forces.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Representatives from the SAF also attend international defence safety conferences, in order to share experiences and also to gain insights on safety benchmarks and practices.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: These are then put into reviews and revisions of safety standards to further enhance them where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The 3rd ERPSS, which began its three-year term in 2021, noted that the SAF had comprehensive systems to ensure the safety and health of our soldiers during training.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This assessment was made after the Panel visited key SAF training schools and an overseas training exercise over the past two years.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about audit findings and learning points.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The system enhances commanders' awareness and decision-making, in order to better prevent accidents.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: The SAF will continue to invest resources and harness technology to strengthen our safety culture.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This concludes my update on the implementation of initiatives in our priority areas.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Work in these areas will never end and we will continue to look for new ways to strengthen the NS system and recognise our NSmen.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: With that, I am now pleased to make two announcements.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: First, in an effort to improve NS processes further, we have reviewed exit controls for NSmen and concluded that we are able to further relax them.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: This change reflects the growing mobility of Singaporeans, with many of our NSmen staying or working overseas for longer durations.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: More details will be announced in due course.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: We hope that this effort – to build this hub and enhance our services to NSmen – will cater even better to the leisure needs of a younger generation of NSmen.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: Mr Chairman, we need an effective NS in order to safeguard our security and our sovereignty.

speaker: Mr Heng Chee How
text: We must build on the contributions of previous generations, take care of our NSmen and ensure that NS is well-positioned to safeguard our way of life into the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister for Defence Dr Ng Eng Hen and Senior Minister of State Mr Heng Chee How spoke at some length about the importance of investing steadily in a strong defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They stressed the importance of long-term investments in building up our military capabilities and strengthening our NS system, even during times of relative peace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I would add that we also need steady investment in Singaporeans' commitment to defence and our collective national resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This underpins our Total Defence philosophy that we started in 1984.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Total Defence has helped us through crises in the past and the most recent COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It is even more needed now to prepare all Singaporeans to withstand ongoing disruptions, to defend against the multitude of threats that lie ahead and for us to continue to thrive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Looking back on the past year's challenges, the Russia-Ukraine war resonates with me because it shows precisely why Total Defence remains critical for Singapore's survival.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The world has been awed by the sheer courage and ingenuity of Ukrainians in their spirited fight against Russia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Member of Parliament Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim and Ms Denise Phua, as well as others highlighted this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And I think there is much we can learn from how the whole-of-Ukrainian society mobilised for its national defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In an inspiring display of Civil and Psychological Defence, many Ukrainian individuals and businesses have volunteered their civilian support for the military effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the same month that Russia launched its full-scale invasion, a historian began making improvised bulletproof vests for soldiers, by taping sawed-off pieces of ploughshares and cut-up transmission belts from farming machines onto sleeveless dress jackets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Then, local business owners, specialising in everything from furniture to metalwork, came together to properly manufacture bullet-proof jackets sewn with camouflage fabric and tool pouches.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Bullet-proof jackets are common apparel in Ukraine now.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There are reports of farmers wearing them while working fields that are peppered with unexploded munitions, and parents preparing them for children in the event of evacuations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also see the interplay between Military, Civil and Digital Defence in how Ukrainians have applied their computer and information technology expertise to help counter Russia's aerial attacks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To overcome limitations in their air defence system, Ukrainian volunteers worked with military and government officials to develop a mobile phone application that allows civilians to report sightings of incoming drones and missiles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Users only needed to point their device in the direction of the incoming object and press a button, and the application would send a report to the military, who would attempt to intercept the object before it struck.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Demonstrating their social and psychological resilience, millions of Ukrainians have returned home since the war began, despite there being no clear resolution to the conflict in sight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some are men who worked overseas and wanted to enlist to defend their country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Others are seniors, women and children who wanted to rebuild their homes and their communities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Their display of Social and Psychological Defence prompts me to reflect on the strength of our national identity and resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I hope that we never have to come to this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But should crisis arise and the country need us, Singaporeans must stand united and stay to defend our country.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Over the past two years, we have been engaging different groups of Singaporeans to strengthen Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In this spirit, we launched the Total Defence Sandbox last year, to crowdsource proposals from youths to put Total Defence into action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the first round of submissions, we received 77 enthusiastic proposals, and have selected some proposals to implement this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, university students Mr Caleb Tan and Mr Sheng Jiankai drew on their love of crime fiction to propose an immersive Total Defence Murder Mystery Role Play Game to help players learn about our multifaceted threat environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Tan said that through their game, they hoped that young Singaporeans would become more aware of the challenges and limitations that Singapore faces, and feel the urgency to take tangible actions for Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We think that their idea is fresh and engaging, and have partnered them with the SDC to bring their game to life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are looking for more creative contributions from Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our second call for proposals to the Sandbox has just commenced and will run until May of this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, we want to deter crises and conflict.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, when crisis hits, we must be prepared.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Government will spare no effort in our response, but the Government also cannot be everywhere all the time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This is where Singaporeans, all of us, must play our part to pitch in to support national efforts, as well as to take care of each other.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Members Miss Rachel Ong, Miss Cheng Li Hui, Mr Chong Kee Hiong and Ms Denise Phua asked how MINDEF was partnering other agencies and the community to bolster community resilience and civic preparedness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Visitors to the Total Defence Day Commemoration Event also learned about facilities and skills that are essential for civic preparedness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To show people that they can still prepare good food in the event of a shortage of fresh food, the ITE College West served nutritious meals that were cooked using ingredients with long shelf lives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In preparation for water-related emergencies, the Public Utilities Board (PUB) had booths to educate the public on water conservation and flood resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Residents were invited to try out PUB's mobile Water Bag Filling Machine, which can pack five-litre water bags for distribution in the event of water supply disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, this is a lot faster and quicker than what we used to remember – pail carrying and long queues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some activities took place in the Civil Defence Shelter in the Community Centre, which is part of a longstanding shelter programme by the SCDF to protect civilians during natural and man-made disasters, as well as wartime emergencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The SCDF also conducted public demonstrations of critical life-saving skills, such as cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and fire extinguishing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am pretty inspired by how an idea that started in the Total Defence Sandbox evolved into a comprehensive and inclusive community effort with the close support of partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Every Singaporean can build up their crisis preparedness by getting certified with life-saving skills and learning how they should prepare for and respond in emergencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We hope to encourage more people to undertake these actions, and we are working with the People's Association and ITE College West to conduct the exercise with Singaporeans from more walks of life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We are also exploring new and more engaging ways to encourage youths to learn about Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: One way is through the Total Defence Interactive Videos, which are available on the MINDEF and SG101 websites.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The latest video, launched just last month, follows a friendly and comical grandmother and grandson duo as they try to tackle modern challenges such as supply disruptions and fake news.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Viewers role-play as the video characters and make decisions that determine how the story unfolds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Through the videos, we hope that viewers reflect on how their individual choices can create a greater impact in the national context.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: School activities also provide valuable platforms for youths to learn about defence and security issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For example, most of us are familiar with the National Cadet Corps (NCC).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Some of us may have been part of the NCC when we were in school.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I, for one, was an NCC cadet too, at one point.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Like many students over the years, this gave me early exposure to Total Defence and prepared me with relevant skills for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: For some, NCC also seeded aspirations for a career in the military.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Today, we continue this tradition of actively engaging students and are piloting a new programme to empower youths to act in Singapore's Digital Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Students from participating secondary schools, junior colleges and polytechnics were offered hands-on workshops, engagement sessions and competitions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: NS is fundamental to our Military Defence, as outlined by Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In turn, community support is critical for the continued success of NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We established the ACCORD in 1984 to bring together community nodes that represent employers, educational institutions, family members and members of the wider community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: ACCORD has grown tremendously and continues to contribute valuable feedback and proposals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Members Ms Joan Pereira and Dr Wan Rizal asked for updates on ACCORD's initiatives, such as efforts to increase community support for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In the past year, ACCORD actively rallied the community to show appreciation for our NSmen through the We Support NS Campaign.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The campaign garnered discounts and benefits for NSmen at 275 retailers that operate a total of 2,500 outlets across Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: In addition, ACCORD remains passionate about preparing youths and their families for NS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We also wanted to give women a glimpse of what NSmen go through, so that they can better support and advocate for NS and Total Defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With this in mind, ACCORD partnered with the SAF to host another edition of the Women's Boot Camp earlier this month.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Koh Wee Min is an alumni of the 2019 Women's Boot Camp who returned to the most recent Boot Camp to support the camp trainers and share her experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Ms Koh also initiated an NS55 project last year to plot the participating merchant outlets that offered We Support NS deals on a shared Google Map list.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This allowed NSmen and their families to easily search for the deals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I think that she embodies the Total Defence spirit of playing your part, wherever you can.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We all have memories of what it means to play our own part for Singapore's defence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It may be something small, like taking pride in your Uniformed Group school unit achieving a Total Defence Gold Badge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Or maybe something more life-changing, like digging your first shell-scrape in the humid jungle or hearing the buzz of mosquitoes as you are doing your doing your sentry duties or sending your loved one off to Pulau Tekong for Basic Military Training (BMT).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These memories of our achievements and sacrifices are precious threads in the hard-won tapestry of our national identity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We believe in preserving these stories and artefacts across generations, so that we can learn about and reflect on the trials and tribulations that we have undergone as a fledgling nation and military.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Members Mr Lim Biow Chuan and Mr Melvin Yong asked about the plans for our defence and military museums, and what visitors can expect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To bring our Singapore defence story to life and better preserve our heritage, we have set up the Defence Collective Singapore to oversee all our defence and military museums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will help us deliver the best possible visitor experiences and national education programmes at our museums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We have been refreshing our museums to ensure that the exhibition content is up to date, and that the visitor experience is interactive and educational.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The SDC completed a refresh a year ago, with new multisensory and digitally-enhanced exhibits on Singapore's past, present and future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Spanning three floors, the refreshed museum uses multimedia and interactive exhibits to tell the story of the Navy's evolution from its humble beginnings to the professional, competent maritime force that it is today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It will also display real equipment from the Challenger-class submarines for the first time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Our NSmen have defended our land, airspace and seas over the decades, and we want to showcase Singapore's NS story and honour the contributions of our NSmen past and present.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will also progressively refresh the Army and Air Force Museums in the coming years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Collectively, visitorship numbers at our museums have been encouraging with over 400,000 visitors annually spanning our military museums and the SDC.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, as its name suggests, Total Defence remains an all-encompassing, unceasing effort to strengthen ourselves, our communities and our nation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MINDEF will continue to invest in Total Defence, in partnership with fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Total Defence is our best preparation for our best response to, and our best recovery from, the threats of today and tomorrow.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We will withstand whatever comes that our way if every Singaporean steps up to play a part in our defence.
